audit.why: 56.45% over 62 games; Akshan owns levels 1-5 and the lane goes Skill from 6 onward as Sylas's scaling arrives. Chart and text agree.
Lvl 2-3 second shot, Lvl 6 Comeuppance, Youmuu's, and Sylas's 2-item AP-bruiser scaling. Correct four, correct order.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two false mechanics. (1) The page calls Abduct a 'chain-stun' three times — Abduct applies no stun; Riot's text is that Sylas throws his chains and PULLS HIMSELF to the enemy he hits. It is a gap-close, not CC. (2) It attributes healing to Chain Lash — 'his Q drain', 'Q/W drain-heal'. Chain Lash damages and slows only; Kingslayer (W) is the sole heal in the kit.
audit.why: Riot description of Abscond/Abduct: 'Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits.' No CC term appears. Riot description of Chain Lash: 'dealing damage to and slowing enemies' — no heal. Riot description of Kingslayer: 'dealing damage and healing himself against enemy champions.' Telling an Akshan player to fear a stun that does not exist changes how they position, and telling them Q sustains sends the Grievous Wounds timing to the wrong ability.
audit.corrected: Abduct is a 13s self-pull with no stun; it is a projectile, so it can be blocked. Only Kingslayer (W) heals, on 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s — that is the anti-heal target.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Once it's down' with no number for the E that decides every trade.
audit.why: Abscond/Abduct is 13/12/11/10/9s. That is a very long window for an Akshan to poke freely and the page should say so.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds call despite the whole late-game framing being 'he out-heals you'.
audit.why: Kingslayer drops to a 6s cooldown at rank 5 and heals off champions; anti-heal is the item decision, not more lethality.

edits.before: Land E1-into-E2 (Abscond into Abduct) to dash in and chain-stun Akshan out of his Heroic Swing, then drain him down
edits.after: Dash Abscond, recast Abduct to yank himself onto you mid-swing, then heal off Kingslayer (W) while you are pinned

edits.before: Survive the early poke with Q/W drain-heal and scale into a self-sustaining AP bruiser who shrugs off lethality
edits.after: Survive the early poke on Kingslayer (W) heals — only W sustains — and scale into an AP bruiser who ignores lethality

edits.before: Sylas is the stronger raw level-1 melee, so you concede the level with only Q and a single passive shot — last-hit at range and don't trade into his Q drain yet.
edits.after: Sylas is the stronger raw level-1 melee, so you concede the level with only Q and a single passive shot — last-hit at range and stay clear of Chain Lash (Q).

edits.before: Sylas has to walk into your Q range to land his own Q drain, and that's a free trade for you: auto, fire the bonus passive shot, then Avengerang on the way out before his W heal lands. Don't sit in melee hoping to all-in him; he wins the sustained brawl with his drain. The thing that flips this lane is his E — if he hits Abscond into Abduct, dashing in and chain-stunning you out of your Heroic Swing, he gets the full drain combo off. Respect that one cooldown and keep terrain behind you to swing away on.
edits.after: Sylas has to walk into your Q range to land Chain Lash, and that's a free trade for you: auto, fire the bonus passive shot, then Avengerang on the way out before Kingslayer (W) heals him. Chain Lash slows, it does not sustain — only W does. Don't sit in melee hoping to all-in him; he wins the long brawl. What flips this lane is Abscond into Abduct (E), a 13s dash-and-yank that puts him on top of you mid-swing. Respect that cooldown and keep terrain behind you to swing away on.

edits.before: This is your window. Hold E (Heroic Swing) to dodge his Abduct chain-pull, then once it's down, step up and Q-auto-passive him for free; he can't drain through poke he never gets to answer. At 6 your Comeuppance out-ranges him and executes a chipped Sylas, and if he steals it the copy is junk since it scales off bonus AD he doesn't build. Force every trade on his E cooldown and you snowball — just don't dive into his Q/W drain while his chain-stun is back up.
edits.after: This is your window. Hold E (Heroic Swing) to dodge his Abduct pull, then once it is down for 13s, step up and Q-auto-passive him for free; he can't heal through poke he never gets to answer. At 6 your Comeuppance out-ranges him and executes a chipped Sylas, and if he steals it the copy is junk since it scales off bonus AD he doesn't build. Force every trade on his E cooldown and you snowball — just don't walk into Kingslayer (W) range while Abduct is back up.

edits.before: Past two items the lane flips and you need to play around it. Sylas's Q/W drain-heal plus AP items turn him into a self-sustaining bruiser who out-heals your lethality, while your missing-health execute stops landing on a target that refuses to stay low — and one clean E2 chain-pull plus ult-steal ends your squishy frame. Close the game on your first-item spike: roam with W camouflage, pick off side-lane mistakes with Comeuppance, and take objectives before he ever reaches the point where he out-stats you.
edits.after: Past two items the lane flips and you need to play around it. Kingslayer drops to a 6s cooldown and, with AP items behind it, out-heals your lethality outright — buy Grievous Wounds or your execute never lands on a target that refuses to stay low, and one clean Abduct plus ult-steal ends your squishy frame. Close the game on your first-item spike: roam with W camouflage, pick off side-lane mistakes with Comeuppance, and take objectives before he ever out-stats you.

edits.before: Sylas out-scales hard: his Q/W drain-heal and AP items make him self-sustaining while your execute falls off — close before late game or a single landed E into ult-steal ends you.
edits.after: Sylas out-scales hard: Kingslayer (W) heals off you every 6s at rank 5 with AP behind it, so buy Grievous Wounds — or close it before a landed Abduct into ult-steal ends you.

notes: Abduct was described as a chain-STUN in three places. It has no CC — it pulls Sylas to you. An Akshan player who thinks he will be stunned mid-swing plays the whole lane wrong. Also moved the heal attribution off Chain Lash onto Kingslayer, which is where Grievous Wounds actually matters.
